title: Colacasia: modeled ₹641/qtl left, Kattappana → Thrippunithura
summary: March 2024: reported colacasia prices at Kattappana and Thrippunithura imply a positive modeled margin after costs on 75% of 20 matched days; a morning-report back-test averages ₹641 per quintal. No actual trade verified.
why_selected: Selected from 194 same-variety market pairs screened for colacasia in March 2024; best tested candidate among the bounded set of routed finalists, not a global optimum.

evidence.observations: daily modal prices for the same variety and grade (FAQ) at both markets; sale matched to the first Thrippunithura report 1–3 days after purchase
caveats: Back-test on reported prices: no actual shipment, buyer or seller is claimed.
Modal prices are reported daily aggregates, not offers anyone could be sure to get.
This data has no arrival volumes, so it cannot show whether the destination could absorb more supply; no capital-constrained or volume allocation optimum is claimed.

Costs extrapolate onion survey values (including to other crops) plus stated allowances, not freight quotes; OSRM car routing, not a verified truck route. Representative town points may not be at mandi gates.
Historical: this says what paid then, not what pays today.

scenes.headline: March 2024
scenes.caption: Kattappana (Kerala) and Thrippunithura (Kerala) both reported colacasia prices for the same variety and grade (FAQ) on 20 matched days.

scenes.headline: Two markets, two prices
scenes.caption: Kattappana reported a median ₹5,500 per quintal. Thrippunithura reported a median ₹6,700 around modeled arrival days. These are not offers.

scenes.headline: Gap ₹1,200/qtl
scenes.caption: The median gap was ₹1,200 per quintal, and Thrippunithura was dearer on 100% of days.

scenes.headline: 116 km by road
scenes.caption: 116 km on OpenStreetMap roads (~2 hours by car). A loaded truck is slower, so we allow 1 days plus 7 days to get paid.

scenes.headline: After modeled costs
scenes.caption: Freight ≈₹25/qtl, 5% fees and commission, loading, 5% loss and interest. On the typical day ₹456 per quintal was left.

scenes.headline: Still positive under stress
scenes.caption: With 25% dearer freight, 10% loss and costlier credit, the typical day still kept ₹122 per quintal.

scenes.headline: A trader who only knew the morning's news
scenes.caption: Using only the latest available Thrippunithura report, the rule selects 16 of 20 modeled shipping days. 13 had positive modeled net, averaging ₹641 per quintal (₹292 under stress).

scenes.headline: The back-test
scenes.caption: The modeled Colacasia route from Kattappana to Thrippunithura was positive on 75% of matched days in March 2024. At that average, a 100-quintal (10-tonne) load implies ₹64,100, or ₹29,200 under stress. Actual buyer, capacity, haggling, rejection and delays are unknown.

assumptions.value: onion survey freight applied per quintal to colacasia
scaled by road km against the 1,115 km Lasalgaon→Azadpur route → ₹25/qtl here
12% a year (14% adverse) for transit + 7 days
~450 road km a day → 1 days here

conclusion: The modeled Colacasia route from Kattappana to Thrippunithura was positive on 75% of matched days in March 2024. At that average, a 100-quintal (10-tonne) load implies ₹64,100, or ₹29,200 under stress. Actual buyer, capacity, haggling, rejection and delays are unknown.

title: Colacasia: modeled ₹1,224/qtl left, Perumbavoor → Athirampuzha
summary: December 2024: reported colacasia prices at Perumbavoor and Athirampuzha imply a positive modeled margin after costs on 100% of 25 matched days; a morning-report back-test averages ₹1,224 per quintal. No actual trade verified.
why_selected: Selected from 168 same-variety market pairs screened for colacasia in December 2024; best tested candidate among the bounded set of routed finalists, not a global optimum.

evidence.observations: daily modal prices for the same variety and grade (FAQ) at both markets; sale matched to the first Athirampuzha report 1–3 days after purchase
caveats: Back-test on reported prices: no actual shipment, buyer or seller is claimed.
Modal prices are reported daily aggregates, not offers anyone could be sure to get.
This data has no arrival volumes, so it cannot show whether the destination could absorb more supply; no capital-constrained or volume allocation optimum is claimed.

Costs extrapolate onion survey values (including to other crops) plus stated allowances, not freight quotes; OSRM car routing, not a verified truck route. Representative town points may not be at mandi gates.
Historical: this says what paid then, not what pays today.

scenes.headline: December 2024
scenes.caption: Perumbavoor (Kerala) and Athirampuzha (Kerala) both reported colacasia prices for the same variety and grade (FAQ) on 25 matched days.

scenes.headline: Two markets, two prices
scenes.caption: Perumbavoor reported a median ₹5,500 per quintal. Athirampuzha reported a median ₹7,500 around modeled arrival days. These are not offers.

scenes.headline: Gap ₹2,000/qtl
scenes.caption: The median gap was ₹2,000 per quintal, and Athirampuzha was dearer on 100% of days.

scenes.headline: 64 km by road
scenes.caption: 64 km on OpenStreetMap roads (~1 hours by car). A loaded truck is slower, so we allow 1 days plus 7 days to get paid.

scenes.headline: After modeled costs
scenes.caption: Freight ≈₹14/qtl, 5% fees and commission, loading, 5% loss and interest. On the typical day ₹1,312 per quintal was left.

scenes.headline: Still positive under stress
scenes.caption: With 25% dearer freight, 10% loss and costlier credit, the typical day still kept ₹931 per quintal.

scenes.headline: A trader who only knew the morning's news
scenes.caption: Using only the latest available Athirampuzha report, the rule selects 25 of 25 modeled shipping days. 25 had positive modeled net, averaging ₹1,224 per quintal (₹856 under stress).
